newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Turkish defence minister on Israeli visit.
newsitem.headline: Turkish defence minister on Israeli visit.

text.p: Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan began a visit to Israel on Wednesday as part of increasing defence cooperation.
The trip was a further blow to the prestige of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who won elections 16 months ago partly on a promise to cut military ties to the Jewish state.
Tayan, from the secularist wing of Erbakan's coalition government, held talks with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
Turkey and Israel have signed defence cooperation agreements which drew an angry response from Iran and many in the Arab world. Israeli planes have flown training flights in Turkey under the accords.
While in Israel, Tayan is to visit Israel Aircraft Industries, which is modernising Turkey's F-4 jet fighters. He is due to return to Turkey on Friday.
Turkey's anti-Islamist army, one of the country's most influential bodies, is pushing Erbakan to curb religious activism.
